# 外貌·服饰·外观 {.unnumbered}



> 本主题共 8 篇语境短文。每篇把一批旧词织进一个场景；目标词**加粗**，展开"本篇生词"可遮释义自测。



### 镜前一瞥——外貌、服饰与颜色

The gallery opening was tonight, and Margot stood before the full-length mirror, making final adjustments. She was **slim** and **neat**, her dark hair pulled up except for two loose **curl**s that framed her cheekbones. She had gone **bald** through a rough winter of illness the year before, so this new growth felt like a small triumph. Tonight she wore a deep-crimson **gown** that matched the **ruby** brooch pinned at her collarbone. A wide **sash** in ivory crossed her waist, its trailing end brushing the floor. The dress was **clad** in tiny seed **bead**s along the bodice—each one catching the lamp like a **gem**. She tugged the **cuff** of her long glove straight, then pulled on a lace **mitt** for her other hand, an affectation she had borrowed from her grandmother.

From the wardrobe shelf she lifted her **cap**—a fitted velvet thing with a gold **rim** around its **brim**—and settled it at an angle. The **wig** she had worn during treatment hung on its stand nearby, retired but not thrown away. On the **rug** beside the dresser sat the small overflow of the evening's accessories: a pair of earrings, a **vase** of dried lavender keeping them company.

Her stylist, a quietly **posh** woman named Sol, had called the overall look "a **swag** of **hues**"—plum, ivory, and that ruby red cycling through the layers. Margot thought that was overblown, but she accepted the compliment. Sol had also done something clever with the **hood** of Margot's travel wrap—tucking it under the collar so the **hind** panel draped in a clean line rather than bunching. The **robe** she'd throw over everything for the cab ride was a generous, unstructured wrap in ecru wool, **trim** and unsentimental.

Outside waited her companion, Danilo—a genuine **hunk** in a tailored navy jacket, the kind of man a **maja** painting would have insisted upon as an escort. He was not someone who made a **mess** of his appearance; his pocket square was crisp, his bearing **pied** with confidence and ease. Neither **pale** nor showy, he occupied rooms the way well-chosen furniture does.

Margot dropped her lipstick into her clutch, snapped it shut, and decided she was ready.

### The Stranger at the End of the Hall

The woman who stepped into the dim gallery looked as though she had wandered out of a painting. A long **cloak** the color of **amber** fell from her shoulders, its hem **draped** in heavy folds that pooled slightly on the marble floor. Stitched along the collar ran a narrow **braid** of gold thread — the kind of **decor** that whispers old money without shouting it. At her throat hung a **badge** on a silk ribbon, its surface **waxy** and worn smooth, and above it her face emerged from a deep **hijab** the shade of **beige** linen, not quite a full **veil** but enough to soften every feature into suggestion. Her hair, where it showed at the temples, was **wavy** and shot through with grey, and she wore it without apology.

Beside her stood a man built like a shipping crate — **burly**, **wiry** arms crossed over a plain **denim** jacket, a **vest** of fleece buckled tight beneath it. His jaw carried a thick **ziff** that no razor had visited in weeks, and his skin had the **grimy** patina of someone who worked outdoors in all weather. He was not tall, yet he seemed to **dwarf** the ornate chair next to him, as though the furniture had shrunk in embarrassment. His **gaunt** companion, hollow-cheeked and hollow-eyed, hovered at his shoulder — a person whose whole **getup** read **funky** in the wrong direction: mismatched, worn thin, drained of color. A loose **fluff** of **ivory** fabric served as a scarf, knotted with the kind of careless grace that might pass for style or might simply be exhaustion.

The room itself had been arranged with deliberate **glitz** — chandeliers, gilt frames, **gaudy** swags of velvet — yet the overall effect was undercut by the **filth** gathering in the corners and the single **bulge** in the ceiling plaster where water had pooled and dried and pooled again. A dusty **crown** moulding ran the perimeter, its plaster roses once white, now **waxy** yellow. Silk flowers **adorned** a side table with the hollow cheerfulness of things placed to fill space rather than to please. The two figures stood in the middle of all of it and studied each other, and neither spoke, and the silence **groomed** itself into something almost ceremonial.

### The Fashion Shoot at Dawn

The model arrived in a **tunic** of deep **khaki**, its loose cut softened by a silk **collar** that caught the early light. Around her waist she had tied a linen **corset** — not tight, just structured enough to give the **blazer** above it something to rest against. Her hair, a warm **auburn**, carried a natural **sheen** that no stylist could have faked. She wore no heavy **rouge**, only a pale **tinge** of rose on her cheeks, and a small silver **brooch** pinned above the breast pocket.

The photographer called it a "quiet shoot," yet everything about the setting was quietly **showy**. Velvet **drapes** in burgundy framed the backdrop; a red **carpet** ran to the mark. A rack behind the assistants held **attire** for three more looks: a **floppy** wide-brim hat, linen **braces** dyed indigo, a **beanie** knitted from undyed wool. The second model — **brawny**, **chunky**, the kind of frame catalogues call "athletic" — pulled on a pair of **aprons** for a utility segment, their canvas panels stiff and **filthy** in a deliberately distressed way. The contrast with the first model's **dainty** accessories was entirely intentional.

Between takes the director watched the monitor, frowning. The wide lens made near objects **blurry** at the edges, and one shot rendered the first model's face slightly **pudgy**, her eyelids **puffy** from a short night. "Move her back two steps," he said, voice **slick** and unhurried. He wanted the **exotic** headpiece — a gilded circlet that looked lifted from a foreign court — to read as centrepiece, not distraction; the model should **flaunt** it without the framing collapsing into spectacle. The building's glass **facade** outside reflected a strip of sunrise, and when it crept across the floor it made the **bonnie** circlet glow. He signalled the crew: this was the frame. For a single held second the whole composition felt less like a fashion photograph and more like a small, arranged world that happened to be **exotic**, precise, and entirely itself.

### The Stranger at the Market Stall

The woman was **petite**, barely reaching his shoulder, but she carried herself with a quiet authority. A thick **mantle** of deep **modena** wool draped over her frame, its **fringe** swaying as she moved through the crowded lane. Her hair was cropped into a neat **fringe** above her brows — not at all **shaggy** or unkempt — and her skin held a warm **suntan**, **tinged** with the kind of gold that comes from months outdoors rather than any bottle. She was not **sallow**, not **hollow**-cheeked; she looked fed and well-rested, which made her stand out here.

He was harder to place. A **rugged** face, jaw edged with a tidy **goatee**, wore a **tinted** pair of wire-rimmed glasses that gave his otherwise **glazed** expression something almost deliberate. His **jersey** was faded — not **shabby** exactly, more like honestly worn — tucked loosely into trousers whose **inseam** had been let out at least once. The leather **sandal** on his left foot was cracked along the sole. A dented **helmet** hung from his elbow, **jagged** where it had once met asphalt.

The stall itself belonged to a third figure, **stumpy** and restless, in a **sloppy** button-down that hung off one shoulder. His hair was **greasy** and **frowsy**, his shop front **slummy** at best — a **sticky** folding table stacked with **thongs**, **pantie** sets still in plastic wrap, a few pairs of knock-off sneakers. A silver **streak** ran through his beard, which was otherwise the colour of mud. His fingers were **skinny** but quick, and he eyed the **quaint** brass clasp on her mantle with undisguised interest.

She noticed. She pulled the cloth tighter, its **tinted** lining catching the light, and turned toward the quieter end of the lane.

### The Gala Newcomer

The ballroom hummed with quiet judgment. Near the entrance stood a **bearded** man in a perfectly pressed **tuxedo**, its **velvet** lapels catching the chandelier light. He adjusted a **hairpin** discreetly borrowed from his wife, who beside him wore a silk gown whose **linings** rustled with every step. Her **earring**s — long gold drops — swayed as she turned to survey the room.

A woman in a jade **turban** glided past, her **apparel** immaculate except for one **creased** sleeve she kept tugging down. Nearby, an older gentleman in a **cutaway** coat tried to project **glamour**, though anyone who looked closely could see the **veneer** was thin: his eyes were **haggard**, his knuckles **gnarled**, his cheeks dotted with a stubborn **freckle** or two. Someone had clearly coached him on posture, but not on concealing the **blemish** above his collar.

The young dancer by the bar wore a **leotard** under sheer **drapery**, her bare arms **encased** from wrist to elbow in long gloves. A brass **chevron** pin on her chest caught the light. Her mascara made every **eyelash** look sculpted. Across from her, an anxious **dresser** from backstage — still in **flannel** trousers and **loafers** — was whispering into a headset, oblivious to the **flaunty** socialite beside him who had just begun to **disrobe** her fur stole with theatrical slowness. One guest, wearing a **leotard** — no, wait, that was the dancer again; this one wore **marbled** silk, **hideous** to some, avant-garde to others — reached up to straighten what appeared to be a **toupee** that had shifted a few centimeters to the left. Nobody said a word. Every **garment** in that room was armor, and every face a carefully maintained **veneer** of ease.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

### 更衣室前的最后一眼

She stood before the mirror, adjusting her **bouffant** hair and slipping a **barrette** into place. Her **stature** was modest, yet everything about her tonight felt heightened—the **dazzling** **sequins** on her gown caught every angle of light, and the **vibrant** **burgundy** fabric pooled slightly at her feet. A **gossamer** shawl draped over her bare shoulders, so light it barely registered. She touched up her **mascara**, pressed her lips together, then misted **perfume** along her collarbone. The **brunette** in the glass looked back with a quiet, **alluring** confidence—**gorgeous**, even to herself.

Earlier it had taken some effort. The first dress she tried was too **prickly** against her skin; the second had gone **crumpled** at the hem. She'd dug through the closet past a worn **singlet**, an old pair of **dungaree** trousers, a forgotten **muffler**, and the **mittens** she never wore. She'd found her **bracelet** beneath a tangle of **panties** and discarded **pajamas**, and unearthed the **necktie** she'd once borrowed from her brother. For a moment she held the tie up against the mirror and laughed—a **raucous**, too-loud sound in the quiet room.

Now she was ready. The heels gave a **squeaky** protest on the polished floor as she crossed toward the door. The corridor light fell across her at a **sloping** angle, casting soft shadows over the faint **freckles** on her nose. Her look was **splashy** and deliberate, **cosmetic** choices made with precision, and the overall effect was nothing short of **airtight**. Whatever the evening held, she was dressed for it.

### The Man by the Boutique Window

The **imposing** figure outside the boutique stopped more than a few passersby. He wore a sharply **tailored** charcoal suit — the kind a master cutter assembles by hand — over a deep-blue **overpull** that gave his broad **physique** a clean, architectural silhouette. A short **mustache** — practically a **mustachio** — traced his upper lip with old-world precision. Around his neck hung a silver **medallion** on a chain that caught the afternoon light.

Inside, the stylist finishing her shift smoothed the **wrinkled** collar of a summer **jumpsuit** on the display mannequin, then straightened a rack of **lingerie** whose lace hems were so fine they were almost **speckled** with light and shadow. She checked her own reflection: **eyelashes** brushed up, a careful swipe of **lipstick**, the **neckline** of her blouse sitting exactly where she'd pinned it. A faint **fragrance** — bergamot and white tea — rose from her wrists. She was, without effort, **glamorous**.

By the door, a young apprentice in paint-stained **overalls** knelt to retie a **shoelace** on his **moccasin**, then stood and reached for the antique **snuffbox** on the shelf — a prop the owner used to date her store. A **stroller** pushed by a tired parent squeaked past the window, the baby inside bundled under a quilted **comforter** that matched the shop's **bedspread** display across the street. The apprentice glanced at the old floor-length mirror leaning against the **wardrobe**: his own face looked back at him — young, no **wrinkles** yet, though a childhood scar near his jaw did **disfigure** the line of his chin slightly. He straightened the canvas strap of his bag — inside it, neatly folded, a **brassière** he was returning for his older sister and a sports **jockstrap** he'd bought for himself. A **pyramidal** stack of shoeboxes beside him cast a sharp shadow across the floor, geometric and deliberate — the whole scene composed, without anyone trying, into something worth watching.

### The Masquerade Night

The ballroom was a **magnificent** **spectacle**. Beneath a **chandelier** dripping with **glittering** crystal arms, guests arrived in masks and costumes, each face a **countenance** half-revealed. A **strapping** man in a velvet cape cut a **conspicuous** figure near the entrance, his **turquoise** cravat catching every flicker of light. Beside him stood a woman whose **curvaceous** silhouette was wrapped in a gown of deep emerald—its fabric subtly **corrugated** at the hem, like the surface of moving water. She wore a **neckerchief** of ivory silk, knotted low, and tucked a folded **handkerchief** into her glove—the kind of detail that separates costume from character. Her hair fell in loose **dreadlocks** threaded with gold wire, **sparkling** with every turn of her head. It was the sort of entrance that goes **out of sight** in memory long before it disappears from the room.

Not everyone dressed to dazzle. One guest arrived in a deliberately **nondescript** coat—no embroidery, no brooch, wholly **unadorned**—yet the deliberateness of it read as its own statement. A small **watermark** logo on the breast pocket suggested the coat was anything but cheap. Near the dessert table, a young attendant wore **suspenders** over a pressed shirt and **panty-hose** the color of champagne, balancing a tray on one arm. The **centerpiece** of the table was a towering arrangement of white orchids and candied fruit, flanked by hand-lettered menus whose opening lines bore a decorative **indentation**. Someone had applied too much **pigmentation** to the painted backdrop behind the table—the gold was almost garish—but in candlelight it merely looked opulent.

The most talked-about guest arrived late. Her complexion was smooth except for a faintly **pockmarked** patch along one jaw, visible only up close and entirely ignored by everyone who mattered. She was **coquettish** without effort—a borrowed **pillow sham** draped over one shoulder as a shawl, a **moisturizer** sheen still fresh on her collarbone. In her hand she carried an old program from a previous year's **masquerade**, folded to mark a page, as if even her props had a story. She was the **centerpiece** no one had planned for—beautiful in the way that needs nothing added and nothing explained.
